transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-27 14:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Recorded: yes
Attendees: Alicia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood PM), Dana (LuminaForge Head of Partnerships), Owen (Platform Eng), Simone (Security), Leo (Product)

[00:00] Alicia: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call — Marcus and I from Redwood, Priya joining to capture any product-level constraints. Dana, Owen, Simone, Leo from LuminaForge?
[00:11] Dana: Yep, all here. Thanks. Wanted to move quickly through the packaging and then deep dive on the runtime pieces.
[00:18] Marcus: Sounds good. I'll start with a quick overview of how Redwood usually packages for marketplace listings — then we can map to LuminaForge's ops.
[00:25] Marcus: So our typical offering has two artifacts: a lightweight listing that points to a container image plus a helm chart for self-managed installs. We also support an operator path but most partners start with helm. The chart includes RBAC templates, K8s resources, and a simple values.yaml that lets you choose between hosted endpoints, Redwood Dedicated, or an on-prem runtime.
[00:45] Owen: Just to clarify — when you say "container image," are we expected to host the image in our registry or do you support pull-through from Redwood's registry?
[00:52] Marcus: Both patterns are supported. For marketplace listing we prefer partners to host the image in their registry and use image signing (cosign) with attestation. We can also provide a signed image from Redwood in certain co-managed cases.
[01:07] Simone: On the security side we need to validate the signing flow and KMS integration. Does Redwood require customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for private deployments?
[01:17] Marcus: For Redwood Private and Dedicated, we integrate with customer KMS — KMS or HSM — yes. For the hosted listing, the control plane may use Redwood's keys but we support envelope encryption with customer keys for data at rest. There's some nuance: if you need HSM-backed keys for attestation, that's something we'll validate with our security team.
[01:35] Leo: For our compliance team it's important that the listing can be deployed into our customer's VPC and that we can pass through SAML assertions for SSO to the console.
[01:44] Priya: We have a marketplace pattern that includes SAML integration for the management console and an RBAC mapping layer. The helm chart exposes a pluggable SSO adapter; we can provide sample SAML config and a template.
[01:56] Dana: Great. On billing and metering — how granular is the meter when deployed through the marketplace? We have two SKU models: per-instance reserved, or usage-based per token for hosted.
[02:06] Marcus: Marketplace metering usually depends on the marketplace vendor. For our standard integration we provide two flavors: a metered usage webhook for token-level billing, or a monthly seat/instance reporting endpoint. We provide reporting hooks and a CSV export; for tighter integrations we can add custom billing events.
[02:22] Owen: Will we need to run any special telemetry agents to get token-level counts?
[02:26] Marcus: No special agent. The runtime emits token counts and request metadata to a metrics endpoint; the helm chart wires a sidecar that batches and ships events. If you want token-level per-customer tagging we'll need to pass the tenant headers from the platform.
[02:39] Simone: Quick question — for image attestation, you said cosign. Do you also support sigstore-based provenance attestation? Our compliance prefers full provenance.
[02:49] Marcus: We can accept sigstore attestations; our release pipeline integrates with Cosign and Rekor. We'll include the recommended provenance format in the checklist.
[02:57] [00:03:00] Dana: Ok can we talk about runtime compatibility? Our platform currently runs mixed nodes — x86 with A100s and a small set of H100s for customers that request it, plus a couple of AMD MI300 nodes in staging. We need to be sure the model builds you recommend run across these.
[03:20] Marcus: Important detail. Redwood's runtime has multi-arch kernels and supports common quantization profiles. We usually publish a compatibility matrix: sequence length, recommended batch sizes per GPU family, and whether to use float16 vs int8 kernels. For AMD MI300 there are a few kernels that are still experimental; we'd want to run a tiny benchmark.
[03:38] Owen: Benchmark would be great. We can carve out a 24-hour window in staging. What should the workload be?
[03:44] Marcus: If you can provide two workloads: (1) low-latency chat (approx 512 token window) and (2) batch embeddings for 1536 token inputs. That will exercise both streaming low-latency paths and batch throughput.
[03:56] Leo: Do you have recommended model variants for cost-sensitive customers?
[04:00] Marcus: Yes — we usually suggest a performance tier (FP16, larger context) and a cost tier (int8 quantized). Redwood Optimize can recommend the quantization profile and expected cost delta. We'll put those profiles in the checklist.
[04:11] [00:04:20] Simone: On encryption and key management — for marketplace deployments some customers demand that private keys never leave their KMS. How does token caching or KV cache encryption work in that scenario?
[04:25] Marcus: The KV cache can be encrypted at rest and we support envelope encryption where the customer-managed KMS only holds the data keys. The runtime never exports plaintext keys; the unsealing happens locally in the node's runtime and keys are rotated per policy. We'll share our KMS integration docs.
[04:40] Dana: Any gotchas around network egress or connectivity when a listing is deployed into a customer's VPC? Guardrails, NATs, etc?
[04:47] Marcus: The main thing is outbound webhook endpoints for billing/telemetry and optional callbacks to Redwood-hosted services for model fallback. We support a fully air-gapped install but that requires shipping the model artifacts and disabling outbound health checks. Standard installs need at least one egress route to the metrics endpoint.
[05:04] Owen: About model fallback — if a customer wants to fallback to Redwood Hosted for spikes, how is traffic routed?
[05:10] Marcus: We have a routing shim in the helm chart that respects a policy — local preferred, fallback to a compatible hosted variant. It also supports weights for A/B style rollouts.
[05:20] [00:05:40] Leo: Can you explain the listing security review process for marketplace certification? We've had previous vendors fail due to missing attestation or insufficient audit logs.
[05:29] Priya: From Redwood's side the flow is: we run a pre-cert checklist (image signing, provenance, RBAC, telemetry), then an optional penetration test if the marketplace requires it, and finally a governance review. We'll share the exact gating doc.
[05:43] Simone: Does Redwood provide the audit log format? Our SIEM needs a particular JSON schema for events.
[05:49] Marcus: Yes we can provide a mapping or an example events export. We'll include a sample Splunk/ELK JSON payload.
[05:57] [00:06:00] Dana: One operational question — for upgrades, do you support in-place rolling updates of the runtime with zero-downtime KV cache migration?
[06:06] Marcus: We support rolling upgrades. KV cache migration is controlled via a compatibility flag; usually we rehydrate caches and support golden path fallbacks. There can be a small warmup latency during the first traffic after upgrade.
[06:18] Owen: For the pilot, what's the recommended minimum cluster size?
[06:21] Marcus: For a pilot with one low-latency and one batch workload, we'd recommend at least 2 GPU nodes: one A100/H100 for latency and one for batch throughput. If you want to mimic multi-tenant behavior add a smaller CPU node for control plane services.
[06:35] [00:06:40] Simone: Any special requirements for FIPS or HSM integrations? We use a vendor that requires PKCS#11 interface.
[06:44] Marcus: We support PKCS#11 for HSMs in the private deploys; for marketplace listing you can document the HSM connector and we'll validate in the pre-cert.
[06:52] Dana: What about commercial terms on the marketplace listing — revenue share, discounts, support SLAs — can we align on a standard?
[06:58] Alicia: I'll push a standard listing term sheet — it's our usual marketplace msla and revenue share templates. We can treat custom requests as addenda.
[07:07] [00:07:10] Leo: Any known edge cases when the partner wants to enable model fine-tuning on-prem?
[07:13] Marcus: Fine-tuning on-prem introduces data locality and checkpoint storage complexity. We support training-light use cases (adapter-based fine-tuning) but full-finetuning would require additional storage and possibly different kernel paths. For marketplace listings we generally recommend inference-only packages unless you explicitly want a training offering.
[07:30] Owen: Ok that helps.
[07:33] [00:07:40] Dana: Let's do a quick timeline — would a mid-December pilot be reasonable?
[07:39] Alicia: If you can get the shortlist of workloads and cluster inventory by Dec 1, we can aim for a rolling pilot starting Dec 8 with a 2-week validation window.
[07:47] Dana: Sounds good.
[07:48] [00:08:00] Marcus: I'll attach the packaging checklist, the helm chart sample, and the quantization profiles to the follow-up. Also the KMS integration doc and the provenance example.
[08:00] Simone: We'll need to confirm whether our compliance requires a third-party pen test before listing. If so we'll alert you.
[08:06] Priya: Noted — we'll hold a follow-up SOC2/HSM session if needed.
[08:11] [00:08:20] Dana: Anything else?
[08:23] Leo: One last: on-region availability — some of our enterprise customers require EU-only deployments. Is there any restriction on region-specific packaging?
[08:31] Marcus: No restriction; the chart is region-agnostic. For regional listing you just pick the image registry and KMS region. We'll document best practices for data residency in the checklist.
[08:43] [00:08:50] Dana: Great. Thanks all.
[08:52] Alicia: Quick recap — Marcus sends artifacts, LuminaForge provides workloads and cluster inventory, Simone flags compliance items, and Alicia follows up on legal. We'll sync again once artifacts are shared.
[09:05] Meeting end.
